name: Business Registration and Investor Resident Card

requirements.blocker_text: Republic of Congo's Investment Charter (Loi n° 2003-06 du 18 janvier 2003) lets a National Investment Commission approve ('agrément') a company for charter tax/customs benefits (Article 15), but the charter's own text sets NO minimum capital threshold and contains NO provision granting a residence permit or visa benefit to the investor -- 'agrément' is a business-registration status, not an immigration status. This dataset could not confirm any dedicated investor-residency track separate from the general resident-card ladder (see cg_long_term_residence.json); a foreign business owner would need to separately qualify for an ordinary or privileged resident card like any other foreign resident.
requirements.fix_path: Register the company and obtain agrément under the Investment Charter (no minimum capital specified in the charter text itself; implementing regulations exist but were not located), then separately apply for a resident card as a foreign business owner.

evidence_required.document: Investment Commission agrément application (implementing regulation referenced in the charter but not located in this build)

outcome.duration_length: tied to whichever resident card tier is obtained (1-5 years)

sources.title: Droit-Afrique (hosting the official Journal Officiel text) -- Loi n° 2003-06 du 18 janvier 2003 portant Charte des investissements: agrément process (Art. 15), no stated capital minimum, no residence-permit provision

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Congo-Brazzaville). STATUS: DRAFT -- the charter text itself is tier 2 (a legal-database host reproducing the official gazette text, not a .gouv.cg domain, consistent with how this dataset treats Lexivox for Bolivia), but the hard requirement's residency-linkage component relies on the tier-3 residence-card-ladder finding (legavox), which caps this file at draft. GENUINE, DISCLOSED ABSENCE (joining the Bolivia/Angola/Cameroon pattern): no confirmed minimum investment threshold, and here additionally no confirmed investor-specific residence benefit at all -- the Investment Charter is purely a business-incentive instrument, not an immigration one, as far as this build could confirm. Openshores mentions a vague 'Investor/Special Economic Zone (Pointe-Noire)' program for energy/forestry/agriculture with 'accelerated processing available,' but gives no threshold or legal basis, so it is not modeled as a separate route here -- it is not distinguishable from ordinary business registration on the evidence found.
